_doc: Schema: see docs/reference/api-parity-ledger/SCHEMA.md — the one home for what
a row means. Do NOT copy it back here; issue 1095 is what that cost.
NOTE (phase-379 W5, 2026-08-27) -- the C++ policy enums MATCH rclcpp's by name
now (`nros::ReliabilityPolicy` and its three siblings, at namespace scope), so
they no longer carry rows. Two differences the report cannot see, recorded here
because nothing else would hold them:
* OUR ENUMERATOR SET WAS SMALLER, AND IS NOT ANY MORE (phase-444, issue
1437). This bullet used to read "rclcpp's four enums each carry
`SystemDefault` and `Unknown`; we decline both", with the reasons:
`SystemDefault` means defer to the middleware and there is none to defer
to (RFC-0036), and `Unknown` is a discovery artefact for a policy read
off a REMOTE endpoint, which we do not do. The first was true of a
REQUEST and a `QoS` is no longer only a request -- `get_actual_qos()`
hands one back. The second was simply wrong about what `Unknown` is: it
is what `rmw_*_get_actual_qos` owes for a policy the backend looked at
and cannot determine on the LOCAL endpoint, which `rmw_vtable.h` has
always said and no implementation anywhere wrote until issue 1437.
Both are now enumerators of all four `nros::*Policy` enums and of the
four `nros_qos_*_t` the C API ships, appended, never renumbered.
PREFIXED there (`ReliabilityUnknown`, not `Unknown`) because ours are
unscoped enums at namespace scope and rclcpp's are `enum class`; and
`LivelinessSystemDefault` is absent because `LivelinessNone` IS
discriminant 0, the sentinel's own value.
WHAT IS STILL DECLINED is `cpp:SystemDefaultsQoS`, the all-sentinel
PRESET (issue 0829: two RMWs resolve it to depth 1 and depth 42). A
value a backend may REPORT is not a profile a caller may REQUEST, and
no public setter can produce a sentinel -- only `detail::qos_from_ffi`,
which is a friend for the read-back direction alone.
Ours also has one rclcpp lacks, `LivelinessManualByNode`, which rmw
deprecated.
* OURS ARE UNSCOPED `enum`, rclcpp's are `enum class`. No row settles this, so
W5 did not switch: an unscoped enum accepts BOTH `nros::Reliable` (ours,
historical, ~10 in-tree uses) and `nros::ReliabilityPolicy::Reliable`
(rclcpp's), where `enum class` would accept only the second and break every
unqualified use site. A scoped-enum switch is its own decision and needs its
own row.
